data.title: Entain in talks to sell remainder of CEE business to CVC, Sky News reports
data.description:
Ladbrokes owner Entain is in advanced talks to sell its remaining stake in its central and eastern Europe operations to private equity firm CVC Capital Partners in a deal that could value the division at between £1.5 billion and £1.75 billion ($1.96 billion to $2.29 billion), Sky News reported on Saturday, citing sources.

Here are some details:

  • Entain holds a 47.5% stake in the CEE business, having offloaded a 20% interest to joint venture partner EMMA Capital in June for €425 million ($466.1 million)

  • Entain said at the time it would keep evaluating options to fully exit the business, which owns SuperSport in Croatia and STS in Poland

  • According to Sky, there are other interested parties

  • Entain is under pressure to cut costs to offset increases in Britain's gambling taxes. It expects an extra £25 million hit to its UK and Ireland retail business after the government raised taxes on the industry for a second consecutive year in last month's budget

  • Entain declined to comment on the report, while CVC did not immediately respond to a request for comment sent outside regular business hours

($1 = 0.7645 pounds)

data.title: The Danger of Jensen Huang's Handshake Deals at Nvidia — WSJ
data.description:
By Tim Higgins

For investors, the most worrisome thing about the entire Jensen Huang scandal isn't the sexiest stuff.

Not the mistresses. Not the suspected Chinese spying. Not the notion of his returning to Nvidia as CEO after he resigned in disgrace.

It's the suggestion that one of the most valuable, most important companies was conducting major deals between suppliers and customers on handshake agreements with Huang — and not with traditional contracts.

"Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," Elon Musk, a major customer of Nvidia chips through his SpaceX and Tesla businesses, recently posted on X. "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."

Such comments help explain motivations of the powerful insiders pushing for Huang's return. They aren't only showing loyalty to the man who could once make or break their companies' growth ambitions, they're trying to ensure their special connections can live on.

At stake is nothing short of the U.S. economy, which has seen a massive boost from artificial-intelligence investment with Nvidia's AI chips and Huang's dealmaking at the center. Without Huang's magic to keep it alive, some worry what will happen next. That's why those, such as Musk, President Trump and others, say Huang should get a pass on his missteps and be allowed back.

Effectively, they're arguing, Huang is bigger than the institution. He's too big to fail.

The dynamic highlights a divide in corporate governance philosophy playing out in public. A New Boys Club of pro-founders is bucking traditional safeguards and limits for the sake of growth, while others embrace more traditional corporate governance, understanding why those rules are there in the first place: continuity.

The very idea of a publicly traded company, after all, is about shared ownership, not a single irreplaceable person.

"Founders are unbelievable in the sense that they create something from nothing — so that is pretty magical," Satya Nadella, one of two chief executives to follow Microsoft founder Bill Gates, said this past week at the New York Times DealBook Summit. "Yes, they're singular, but they're not gods." He added, "As I used to say to Bill, founders also die so at some point a company, if it needs to succeed, it has to have someone take over."

To be fair, Nvidia's remaining leadership team is arguing they can carry on without their founder. The AI chip company does rely on contracts as it competes to lock down space among third-party foundries and in-demand memory. On Tuesday, interim CEO Colette Kress tried to alleviate worries as she highlighted Nvidia's purchase commitments of $390 billion.

"It's business as usual," Kress told analysts. "We've engaged with our customers, we've engaged with our suppliers...They're all 100% up behind us." And she even name-checked Nvidia's most important supplier, TSMC, which makes the chips that the California company designs.

Still, Huang had long celebrated the fact that, for roughly 30 years, he did business with TSMC without formal contracts. To him, it was a sign of trust. "I don't know how many tens, hundreds of billions of dollars of business we've done through them and we don't have a contract," he told a podcaster in March. "That's pretty great."

The following month, during another podcast appearance, Huang again touted that relationship. "There's always some rough justice — sometimes I'm right, sometimes I'm wrong, sometimes I got a better deal, sometimes I got a worse deal, but overall the relationship is incredible," he said.

Supporters of Huang's approach say it played to cultural aspects of the Asian supply chain where personal relationships are currency. Or that such approaches allowed Nvidia to move fast to take advantage of a quick-moving technology. And, while Huang may have eschewed big contracts with the likes of TSMC, down in the middling ranks, there would have likely been actual purchase orders to assure quantities and prices were detailed. As microprocessor maestro Patrick Moorhead has argued, those agreements are mostly in place for at least 18 months.

"The real exposure is the next round: anything not on paper, and whether Nvidia keeps committing at Jensen's pace," the Moor Insights & Strategy founder wrote.

Part of Huang's success was the trust he developed throughout the ecosystem as something of a middleman between his technology's upstream suppliers and downstream customers. He helped build that ecosystem in part by locking up capacity with purchase agreements while using more "implicit" means — selling suppliers on a vision for the future that they believed he could deliver.

"For example, a lot of the investments that are upstream are made by our supply chain because I said to the CEOs, 'Let me tell you how big this industry is going to be, let me explain to you why, let me reason through it with you, and let me show you what I see,' " Huang said on the Dwarkesh Podcast.

If anyone should understand the downside to doing business without formal contracts, it should be Musk, who helped found OpenAI with tens of millions of dollars before things eventually turned sour.

His yearslong legal battle with OpenAI revolved around his claims that Sam Altman betrayed him by remaking the AI lab into a commercial venture. OpenAI has argued there was never any contract.

The issue around whether they had an agreement or not was never decided because a jury earlier this year rejected the lawsuit, finding the statute of limitations for bringing a case had expired. At one point during the legal battle, though, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers questioned the wisdom of Musk's pumping money into OpenAI without the terms and conditions in writing.

"It's a lot of money to do on a handshake," she said.

Musk's lawyer, who had argued emails suggested a shared understanding, replied that there was no requirement for a formal contract. "I understand there's no requirement," the federal judge said. "I'm just stating the obvious: $45 million on a handshake and what do you end up with? You end up in...court."

At the very least, you end up with uncertainty — which is what's hanging over Nvidia. Except in this instance, the proposed salve proposed through a public pressure campaign by the New Boys Club is to bring back Huang — a suggestion that, so far, the Nvidia board has rejected.

On Wednesday, Musk continued his advocacy for Huang, arguing he is irreplaceable, in part because of his personal connections. "It's like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you're on a winning streak," Musk said during a remote appearance at the Dealbook conference.

Huang may very well be the Jordan of his time, but that doesn't mean there won't be a LeBron James on the horizon.

Write to Tim Higgins at tim.higgins@wsj.com

data.title: Cohance Lifesciences: USFDA inspects and classifies Telangana facility as ‘voluntary action indicated’
data.description:
The US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) has concluded inspecting Cohance Lifesciences Ltd's formulation manufacturing facility in Shamshabad, Telangana, and it classified as Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI), the company said on November 21.

It was also issued an Establishment Inspection Report (EIR) for the facility.

VAI is an FDA classification indicating that regulatory action is not currently warranted, but the agency has identified issues that call for voluntary corrective action by the establishment. EIR, or Establishment Inspection Report, is the FDA's formal report documenting the findings and outcome of an inspection.

The company had previously informed the exchanges about the USFDA inspection on September 5, 2026. "With the receipt of the EIR, the said inspection stands concluded," Cohance Lifesciences said in a regulatory filing.

Shares of Cohance Lifesciences closed at ₹462.30 apiece on the NSE on Friday, November 20, up 0.62% for the day.

data.title: JNPA awards 8-yr contract to Gateway Distriparks for DFC-compliant common rail yard operations
data.description:
Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA) has awarded an eight-year contract, with an option to extend it by another two years, to New Delhi-based Gateway Distriparks Ltd (GDL) for the operation and management of its Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC)-compliant Common Rail Yard at Nhava Sheva.

The contract covers the operation, maintenance and management of Rail Lines T1 and T2 at the facility, which has been developed at an estimated investment of ₹225 crore, stated an official release here on Saturday. Spread across 15.9 hectares, the rail yard is equipped with two 1,500-metre-long DFC-compliant railway lines and an engine escape line, enabling it to handle long-haul, double-stack container trains carrying up to 720 TEUs per rake.

The common rail yard is expected to streamline container movement between the Dedicated Freight Corridor and JNPA’s five container terminals — NSFT, NSICT, APMT, NSIGT and BMCT — by providing a centralised facility for handling and segregation of container trains. Currently, around 96 per cent of container trains arriving at JNPA carry mixed cargo destined for multiple terminals, resulting in operational complexities and additional handling requirements. The new facility is aimed at addressing these challenges through centralised train handling, container segregation and inter-terminal transfers.

Under the agreement, GDL will undertake end-to-end rail yard operations, including train placement, loading and unloading, lashing and unlashing of single- and double-stack rakes, segregation of mixed container trains, yard stacking and inter-terminal container movement. JNPA Chairperson Gaurav Dayal said the award of the contract marks another step towards improving the port’s rail connectivity and ensuring faster, more reliable cargo movement. He added that the common rail yard would facilitate seamless movement of containers between the DFC network and port terminals, while supporting JNPA’s broader objective of increasing the share of rail-based cargo transportation.

The operator will deploy a fleet of reach stackers and GPS-enabled internal transfer vehicles (ITVs), integrated with a web-based Terminal Operating System (TOS), to enable real-time cargo visibility for terminals, railways and other trade stakeholders.The facility is also expected to strengthen JNPA’s ability to attract container cargo from the northern hinterland, including the National Capital Region, Punjab, Rajasthan, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. With improved DFC integration, the port aims to benefit from faster transit times and lower per-TEU logistics costs, potentially helping it regain its historical 30 per cent share of container cargo from the northern hinterland.

GDL is scheduled to mobilise equipment and commence operations at the facility within one month of the issuance of the work order.

data.title: Nordic Fibreboard AS unaudited financial report for the Q3 of 2026
data.description:
MANAGEMENT REPORT

Nordic Fibreboard AS consolidated net revenue in Q3 2026 was €2.71 million, representing a 36% increase compared to the same period of the previous year (Q3 2025: €1.99 million), revenue increased by €723 thousand. The Group's main business activity is the production and wholesale of fibreboard, which accounted for the vast majority of the Group's revenue in Q3 2026. The second segment comprises the management of the property located on Suur-Jõe Street in Pärnu. However, following the termination of the lease agreements for the building in August 2024, the revenue generated by this segment is immaterial.

Nordic Fibreboard's operating EBITDA in Q3 2026 was positive €134 thousand, with an EBITDA margin of positive 5% (Q3 2025 EBITDA: positive €94 thousand, EBITDA margin: positive 5%). The results for the third quarter of 2026 were positively impacted by increases in the selling prices of our products and relatively low natural gas prices. Unfortunately, natural gas prices have increased since September. In September, the market price of natural gas was EUR 61.4/MWh, compared to EUR 85.4/MWh in November. The market price has temporarily even exceeded EUR 100/MWh. Operating EBITDA for the fourth quarter is expected to remain significantly negative. Should the conflict in the Middle East escalate, natural gas prices are expected to rise considerably from their current levels. We are seeking to increase the selling prices of our products, but these adjustments take time. Due to existing contracts and the competitive environment, we are unable to increase our selling prices as quickly as natural gas prices rise.

In addition to Nordic Fibreboard's consolidated operating EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026, the Group recognised one-off income of €400,000. This amount represents an advance payment received in connection with the planned sale of the Admirali quarter (Suur-Jõe 48 property and the adjacent 10 properties), which was retained by Nordic Fibreboard as the sale did not take place.

Financial expenses in Q3 2026 were €92 thousand, consisting of loan interest costs and other financial costs (€43 thousand in Q3 2025).

The Group's consolidated net profit for Q3 2026 was €292 thousand (Q3 2025 net loss: €77 thousand), of which EUR 400,000 resulted from the termination of the preliminary sale-purchase agreement for the Admirali quarter (Suur-Jõe 48 property and the adjacent 10 properties). The Group's consolidated net loss for the first nine months of 2026 was €692 thousand (net loss of €574 thousand in the first nine months of 2025).

Fibreboard production and sales

Revenue from fibreboard sales amounted to €2.71 million in Q3 2026, compared with €1.99 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of €723 thousand, or 36%. The improvement in sales performance was primarily supported by sales to new customers.

Nordic Fibreboard Ltd OÜ’s EBITDA for Q3 2026 was positive EUR 153 thousand (Q3 2025 positive EUR 122 thousand). Nordic Fibreboard Ltd OÜ’s net loss for the Q3 of 2026 amounted to €58 thousand (Q3 2025 net loss of €48 thousand). Q3 2026 EBITDA was continued to be impacted by a sharp rise in energy prices (including gas prices nearly doubling from the start of the year), which resulted from the U.S. military strike on Iran at the end of February.

As a secondary activity, the Group owns and manages the Admirali Quarter real estate development project in Pärnu, located on the site of a former furniture factory, for which a detailed plan has been established for residential real estate development. Previously, the Suur-Jõe 48 property was owned and managed by Pärnu Riverside Development OÜ, a wholly owned subsidiary of Nordic Fibreboard AS, however on 30.07.2025 Nordic Fibreboard AS and Pärnu Riverside Development OÜ entered into a merger agreement, under which Nordic Fibreboard AS was the acquiring entity and Pärnu Riverside Development OÜ was the entity being absorbed. The merger date was 01.06.2025 and as a result of the merger, the Suur-Jõe 48 property is now directly owned by Nordic Fibreboard AS.

The design works for the Admirali Quarter development project at Suur-Jõe 48 have been completed. data.title: Dhruv Dhawan To Join Amazon Ads In Leadership Move
data.description:
The digital advertising veteran moves to Amazon after leading India revenue at The Trade Desk, bringing over two decades of industry experience

Dhruv Dhawan is set to join Amazon Ads, marking his next leadership move in India's rapidly evolving digital advertising industry. He most recently served as Vice President – Revenue for India at The Trade Desk, where he joined in April 2025 to lead business development, client partnerships and revenue growth.

Dhawan brings more than 20 years of experience across digital advertising, media, telecommunications, technology and consulting. His expertise spans business strategy, revenue management, advertising solutions, digital transformation and building partnerships with advertisers and agencies.

Before joining Amazon Ads, Dhawan was associated with The Trade Desk, where he led the company's India revenue operations. His responsibilities included expanding business opportunities, strengthening relationships with advertising agencies and brands, and driving growth in the programmatic advertising ecosystem.

Prior to that, he served as Head of Ads at Disney+ Hotstar, where he led the platform's advertising business. His responsibilities covered advertising sales, go-to-market strategy, pricing, content solutions, ad technology partnerships, ad operations and business development across sports and entertainment.

Following the formation of JioStar through the merger of Disney+ Hotstar and Viacom18, Dhawan also took on responsibilities related to building the markets vertical at the combined entity.

Earlier, Dhawan spent more than nine years at Google in various leadership positions, working across industries including telecommunications, financial services, fast-moving consumer goods, consumer packaged goods, automotive and e-commerce. His last role at the company involved leading its FMCG, CPG and direct-to-consumer business.

He began his professional career with Electrolux Kelvinator and subsequently worked at Bharti Airtel in sales, marketing and business leadership roles. He also gained management consulting experience at Accenture.

An alumnus of Symbiosis Institute of Business Management, Dhawan brings experience across the advertising and technology ecosystem, having worked with major digital platforms, media businesses and telecom companies.

His move to Amazon Ads comes as digital advertising platforms compete to expand their presence in India's growing online advertising market. Amazon Ads offers brands advertising solutions across its retail marketplace, streaming services and other digital properties, with an emphasis on connecting advertisers with consumers across multiple touchpoints.

data.title: TCS Hyderabad Office Faces Protest Over Employee Dress Code Dispute
data.description:
An employee alleged he was denied entry for wearing Ayyappa Deeksha attire, triggering protests and raising questions over workplace dress codes

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) faced protests outside its Adibatla office near Hyderabad on November 19 after an employee alleged that he was denied entry for wearing traditional attire while observing Ayyappa Deeksha.

The employee, identified as Manish, who has reportedly been working with TCS for around two years, claimed that he had informed the management nearly two months in advance about his decision to observe the religious vow. However, when he reported to work wearing a traditional mundu and Ayyappa Mala, he was allegedly stopped at the office entrance over the company's dress code.

Manish questioned the decision, alleging that other employees were permitted to enter despite not following the same dress requirements. He also named a senior colleague, Sikender Shah, in connection with his allegations of discriminatory treatment. The allegations have not been independently established.

The incident prompted Ayyappa devotees and members of Hindu organisations to gather outside the company's Adibatla campus, demanding that the employee be allowed to attend work while observing his religious practices. Protesters raised slogans against the management, and police intervened to prevent the gathering from escalating.

According to reports, the disagreement arose after the employee arrived wearing traditional attire associated with the 41-day Ayyappa Deeksha observance, which devotees undertake ahead of the Sabarimala pilgrimage in Kerala.

A senior Adibatla police officer subsequently described the incident as a misunderstanding over workplace attire. According to the officer, the company's HR team had asked the employee to change from his traditional mundu into trousers, reportedly citing concerns that international clients might not be familiar with the attire. The police ruled out a communal angle and said the matter had been resolved.

Police initially said they had not received a formal complaint and were verifying the circumstances surrounding the incident. The situation was later brought under control, with the protests ending following police intervention.

The incident has brought renewed attention to the challenges multinational companies face in balancing workplace dress codes, professional requirements and employees' religious practices.

TCS had not issued an official public statement on the incident in the reports available as of November 21, 2026.

For HR teams, the episode raises questions about how organisations frame and implement workplace appearance policies, particularly when employees seek reasonable accommodation for religious observances. Consistent application of dress codes, transparent communication and clear grievance-redressal mechanisms remain important considerations in managing such workplace disputes.

data.description:
The rally takes NSE’s market capitalisation to approximately Rs 5.5 lakh crore, compared with around Rs 4.4 lakh crore at the issue price

The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has broken into the top five global exchange operators by market capitalisation, overtaking US-based Nasdaq and Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX), as its post-listing rally continues to lift its valuation.

NSE’s market capitalisation reached approximately USD 59.3 billion as of 20 November, compared with around USD 57.7 billion each for Nasdaq and HKEX. The Indian exchange now ranks fifth globally, according to market data, placing it ahead of two established international peers less than two months after its stock market debut.

The global rankings are topped by CME Group, valued at approximately USD 109.6 billion, followed by Intercontinental Exchange, which owns the New York Stock Exchange, at USD 95.5 billion. Germany’s Deutsche Boerse occupies the third position with a market capitalisation of USD 63.7 billion, while London Stock Exchange Group ranks fourth at USD 60.1 billion.

NSE is now just around USD 800 million behind London Stock Exchange Group.

NSE Market Cap Rises Rs 1.1 Lakh Crore Since IPO

The exchange operator’s shares continued their upward trajectory on Friday, trading at Rs 2,222 in afternoon deals, up 1.5 per cent for the session. The stock is now trading 24.5 per cent above its IPO issue price of Rs 1,785.

The rally has taken NSE’s market capitalisation to approximately Rs 5.5 lakh crore, compared with around Rs 4.4 lakh crore at the issue price. This represents an increase of nearly Rs 1.1 lakh crore in valuation in less than two months.

NSE made its stock market debut in September, listing on the BSE at Rs 1,800 per share, a premium of 0.84 per cent over the issue price. Its market capitalisation stood at around Rs 4.5 lakh crore on the listing day.

The IPO was India’s second-largest public offering, behind Hyundai Motor India’s Rs 27,870-crore issue in 2024.

The exchange’s rapid ascent in global rankings marks a significant milestone for India’s capital markets, with NSE now valued above Nasdaq and HKEX despite their established positions in the global financial ecosystem.

data.title: Arohan Financial Services, Pristine Logistics Get Sebi Nod To Advance Rs 600 Cr IPO Plans
data.description:
Sebi’s observations allow Arohan to launch its IPO within 12 months and Pristine within 18 months

Arohan Financial Services and Pristine Logistics & Infraprojects have received regulatory clearance to move ahead with their proposed initial public offerings (IPOs), adding two more companies to the pipeline of firms seeking to tap India’s primary market.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) issued its observations on Arohan Financial Services’ draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) on 13 November, followed by its clearance for Pristine Logistics’ confidential filing on 19 November.

The two companies had taken different routes to approach the regulator. Arohan filed its draft offer document in May 2026 through the conventional route, while Pristine submitted its papers confidentially in June.

Sebi’s observations allow Arohan to launch its IPO within 12 months and Pristine within 18 months. Under the confidential filing mechanism, Pristine will first need to submit an updated DRHP to Sebi and subsequently file its red herring prospectus with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) before opening the issue, subject to regulatory requirements.

Arohan Plans Rs 600 Crore Fresh Issue Cum OFS

Arohan Financial Services, a technology-enabled non-banking financial company (NBFC) focused on microfinance, is planning to raise Rs 600 crore through a fresh issue of shares. The proposed offering includes a pre-IPO placement of Rs 120 crore.

In addition, existing shareholders will offer 4.04 crore equity shares for sale through the offer-for-sale (OFS) component.

The investors participating in the OFS include Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America, Aavishkaar Goodwell India Microfinance Development Company, Tano India Private Equity Fund, Maj Invest Financial Inclusion Fund, Danish Sustainable Development Goals Investment Fund, and Michael and Susan Dell Foundation.

Arohan intends to deploy the net proceeds from the fresh issue towards strengthening its capital base to support future business requirements, including onward lending. A portion will also be used for general corporate purposes.

Pristine Logistics Operates Rail-led Multimodal Platform

Pristine Logistics & Infraprojects operates an integrated logistics platform focused on rail transportation and multimodal infrastructure. Its services cover both containerised and non-containerised cargo, including export-import (EXIM) and domestic container logistics, bulk rail transportation, warehousing, container maintenance and repair, and mining logistics.

The company expanded its mining logistics operations through the acquisition of Sical Logistics.

Pristine is promoted by Amit Kumar, Durgesh Govil, Rajnish Kumar and Sanjay Mawar, who bring experience spanning Indian Railways, Container Corporation of India (CONCOR), rail infrastructure development, logistics and legal services.

Separately, Sebi also issued observations on the IPO offer documents of Advanced Sys-Tek and Assetz during the week, adding to the list of companies progressing towards public listings.

data.title: ECB seeks industry partners for tokenized deposits, securities experiments
data.description:
The European Central Bank (ECB) is seeking financial market participants to help explore tokenized deposits and securities as part of its efforts to build an integrated European financial ecosystem using blockchain technology.

On Friday, the ECB invited industry groups to participate in analytical work and experiments under its Appia initiative, identifying three priority areas, including tokenized deposits and related payments, tokenized securities and shared network governance.

According to the ECB, interested participants must apply as part of a collective initiative comprising independent legal entities rather than individually. Groups can apply for one or more workstreams, with proposals evaluated based on factors including expertise, practical experience, technical readiness and expected contributions.

Applications for the first experimental exercises are due by Dec. 11, while later submissions will be assessed on a rolling basis.

The initiative builds on the Eurosystem’s broader Appia roadmap, which aims to develop a unified European tokenized financial ecosystem anchored in central bank money. The ECB plans to publish a blueprint outlining findings and a proposed framework in 2028.

The invitation comes as ECB President Christine Lagarde warned that Europe risks missing an opportunity to establish an integrated market for tokenized securities if incompatible standards emerge across platforms.

Lagarde urged policymakers to establish common rules to prevent fragmentation as blockchain-based financial infrastructure develops across the region.

data.title: Trump Memecoin Hits 2026 Low As Price Slumps Ahead Of President’s VIP Dinner
data.description:
Key points:
  • TRUMP token is down more than 53% over the past month and about 99% from its all-time high.
  • Trump will host the top 185 holders at his Washington, D.C., golf club, with a VIP reception for the top 29, the Financial Times reported.
  • Democratic lawmakers have vowed to investigate the president's crypto ventures once the new Congress begins in January.

The Official Trump (TRUMP) memecoin slipped on early Saturday, after sliding to its lowest level in 2026, the day before U.S. President Donald Trump was reportedly planning to host a dinner for the token’s biggest holders.

TRUMP's price was down more than 10% in the last 24 hours. It’s down more than 53% in the past month. It has also lost about 99% of its value from its all-time high of $73.43 in January 2025.

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around TRUMP remained in the ‘bullish’ zone, while chatter around it shifted to ‘low’ from ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

The crash came despite a report that Trump was set to host a dinner for the top 185 holders of TRUMP. The top 29 will also get a VIP reception with the president and a celebrity guest. The dinner will take place on Sunday at the Trump National golf course in Washington, D.C., the Financial Times reported on Friday.

Sell-Off Since Midterms

TRUMP has fallen 46% since the midterm elections, the steepest drop among Trump-linked crypto assets.

Other crypto assets tied to the Trump family have also slipped, including the World Liberty Financial (WLFI) token, which was down 14% over that period, and shares of Bitcoin (BTC) miner American Bitcoin (ABTC), co-founded by Eric Trump, which have dropped by 47%, according to FT.

The TRUMP coin and Trump Media & Technology Group (DJT) stock fell the day after the vote, even as the broader market rallied.

Scrutiny Builds In Washington

Democratic lawmakers have said they plan to investigate the president's crypto ventures once the new Congress begins in January. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) and Richard Blumenthal (D-CON.) have vowed to look into past memecoin dinners.

At the time, Trump had pushed back against the planned probes. In a post on Truth Social after the midterms, he called Democrats seeking investigations "extortionists," adding, "This is Weaponization and Lawfare at another level."

This will be the third such event since the memecoin launched in January 2025. In May 2025, Trump hosted about 220 top holders at a gala dinner at his golf club in northern Virginia.

In April this year, nearly 300 holders attended an event at his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida, as the token slid to an all-time low.

data.title: USFDA issues 7 observations to NATCO Pharma's Hyderabad facility
data.description:
NATCO Pharma Limited on Saturday said it has received seven observations from the US health regulator following an inspection of its manufacturing facility in Kothur, Hyderabad.

The US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) conducted an inspection of the company's plant during November 12-20, NATCO Pharma said in a regulatory filing.

Upon conclusion of the inspection, the company received seven observations in Form 483, it added.

In USFDA parlance, a Form-483 is issued to a firm's management at the conclusion of an inspection when investigators observe conditions that, in their judgment, may constitute violations of the laws.

"The company believes that the observations are procedural in nature and is confident of addressing these observations comprehensively within stipulated timelines," NATCO Pharma said.

data.title: Iraq fire at Basra power station kills at least 4, injures 30
data.description:
At least 4 people were killed and 30 injured in a fire at a power station in southern Iraq on Saturday, with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.

Civil defence teams brought the fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra under control after firefighters responded to the incident, Iraq's state news agency, INA, reported.

The fire spread to neighbouring houses and forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said.

The Hartha station has an installed generating capacity of 800 megawatts but had been operating at around 400 megawatts before the fire, they said.

There was no immediate official information on the cause of the fire or the extent of the damage, INA reported.

Iraq's electricity infrastructure has long struggled with decades of underinvestment, inadequate maintenance and an inability to meet peak demand, particularly during the extremely hot summer months. Fires and technical failures at substations and power facilities have previously disrupted electricity supplies and caused widespread outages.

data.title: Dhruv Dhawan Joins Amazon Ads, Exits The Trade Desk
data.description:
The digital advertising veteran moves to Amazon after leading India revenue at The Trade Desk, bringing over two decades of industry experience

Dhruv Dhawan is set to join Amazon Ads, marking his next leadership move in India's rapidly evolving digital advertising industry. He most recently served as Vice President – Revenue for India at The Trade Desk, where he joined in April 2025 to lead business development, client partnerships and revenue growth.

Dhawan brings more than 20 years of experience across digital advertising, media, telecommunications, technology and consulting. His expertise spans business strategy, revenue management, advertising solutions, digital transformation and building partnerships with advertisers and agencies.

Before joining Amazon Ads, Dhawan was associated with The Trade Desk, where he led the company's India revenue operations. His responsibilities included expanding business opportunities, strengthening relationships with advertising agencies and brands, and driving growth in the programmatic advertising ecosystem.

Prior to that, he served as Head of Ads at Disney+ Hotstar, where he led the platform's advertising business. His responsibilities covered advertising sales, go-to-market strategy, pricing, content solutions, ad technology partnerships, ad operations and business development across sports and entertainment.

Following the formation of JioStar through the merger of Disney+ Hotstar and Viacom18, Dhawan also took on responsibilities related to building the markets vertical at the combined entity.

Earlier, Dhawan spent more than nine years at Google in various leadership positions, working across industries including telecommunications, financial services, fast-moving consumer goods, consumer packaged goods, automotive and e-commerce. His last role at the company involved leading its FMCG, CPG and direct-to-consumer business.

He began his professional career with Electrolux Kelvinator and subsequently worked at Bharti Airtel in sales, marketing and business leadership roles. He also gained management consulting experience at Accenture.

An alumnus of Symbiosis Institute of Business Management, Dhawan brings experience across the advertising and technology ecosystem, having worked with major digital platforms, media businesses and telecom companies.

His move to Amazon Ads comes as digital advertising platforms compete to expand their presence in India's growing online advertising market. Amazon Ads offers brands advertising solutions across its retail marketplace, streaming services and other digital properties, with an emphasis on connecting advertisers with consumers across multiple touchpoints.

data.title: India Can Build 600 MT of Steel. Can It Afford to Move, Fuel and Decarbonise It?
data.description:
India has proved it can add steel capacity at speed. But it is building into a world already awash in surplus metal, which means the 600 MT target will be decided less by furnaces than by four lines on the cost sheet: raw materials, logistics, imports, and carbon

India's steel industry has already done what would have looked improbable a decade ago. The country produced about 165 million tonnes (MT) of crude steel in 2025, more than the United States and Japan combined, and the steel ministry puts installed capacity at roughly 220 MT. The official goal is now 300 MT of capacity by 2030-31 and 600 MT of production by 2047.

The timing is what makes that goal hard. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development estimates global steel overcapacity at 640 MT in 2025, rising to 745 MT by 2028, and India was the biggest source of capacity additions in Asia between 2021 and 2025. New Indian tonnes will therefore compete with surplus metal looking for a buyer, some of it already arriving at Indian ports.

Despite a three-year safeguard duty imposed in December 2025, imports have kept coming, with China the largest supplier, and the government is reportedly weighing an extension of the duty. In that market, the question for the next phase of growth is not whether India can build the furnaces. It is whether it can make and deliver steel at a cost that holds up against the world's surplus.

The Logistics Behind 600 MT Steel

The size of the task shows most clearly when 600 MT is counted in raw materials rather than finished steel. D. B. Sundara Ramam, Vice President - Corporate Services at Tata Steel, put the number plainly. He said, “When we talk about 600 million tons of steel, close to more than 2 billion tons of material movement we are talking about, that is iron ore, coal, limestone, dolomite, all collections, more than 2 billion tons. But going by the coal history, today we know that in India more than 1 billion tons of coal is produced and is being transported to the thermal power plants and steel plants also”

But confidence in capability is not confidence in cost. Ramam added that “economically viable supply chain logistics is going to be a critical success factor for achieving our dream of close to 600 million tons of steel production.”

Steel moves iron ore, coal and limestone in on one side and heavy finished product out on the other, and industry has long argued that freight eats a disproportionate share of its margin. In 2020, Jindal Steel and Power's then managing director V. R. Sharma told a FICCI forum that moving finished steel alone cost about Rs 8,000 a tonne and added roughly 28 per cent to factory cost.

Naveen Jindal, President of the Indian Steel Association (ISA) and Chairman of Jindal Steel, said the answer is a wider toolkit. “Better rail connectivity, port infrastructure, coastal shipping, slurry pipelines and integrated logistics network can significantly improve the competitiveness of the industry,” he said.

A Coal Problem Inside An Ore Story

India's cost base is lopsided. Iron ore is plentiful; coking coal is not. The steel ministry told a parliamentary committee in November that about 90 per cent of blast-furnace coking coal demand is met through imports. India brought in about 62.6 MT of coking coal in 2025, nearly 10 per cent more than the year before, and the ministry's own benchmark for Australian coking coal climbed from about USD 175 a tonne in March 2025 to USD 243 in June 2026.

The Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA) calculates that around 64 per cent of the 382 million tonnes a year of capacity now under development is anchored in the coal-based blast-furnace route. The ministry has projected a coking-coal requirement of 161 MT by 2029-30. Every additional blast furnace, in other words, adds to India's exposure to a seaborne price it does not set.

Jayant Acharya, Joint Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of JSW Steel,  argued that both halves of the raw-material problem need policy attention; he said, “The one which I think we need to address and require support is the raw material security again. India is blessed with a lot of iron ore resources. We need to open up more mines. And we need to see that existing mines increase the price. Second is on the raw material side is coking coal. India is dependent on coking coal imports because metallurgical coal in India is high ash. However, domestic coking coal can be mined, washed, and blended. I think there is a big opportunity in doing that. So these two require policy enablers to hasten the process.”

The washing-and-blending route he describes is already official policy. Mission Coking Coal, launched in 2021, targets 140 MT of domestic coking-coal output and a rise in domestic blending in steel from 10 per cent to 30 per cent by 2030. The gap between that ambition and the 161 MT requirement shows why industry wants the process hastened.

Imports And The Quality Gap

Demand gives the industry real room. Ashok Kumar Panda, Chairman and Managing Director of the Steel Authority of India (SAIL), said consumption could reach 170-180 MT this year. Per-capita consumption, which he put at around 108 kg against a global average of around 219 kg, leaves a long runway as infrastructure and the rural economy develop.

But the import data suggests that demand growth alone will not protect Indian mills. Chinese steel accounted for nearly a third of finished steel imports in a recent period, and the government has found itself defending the domestic market with trade remedies even as consumption rises. A tariff can buy time. It cannot lower a mill's cost of production.

Panda argued that the industry should stop treating scale and efficiency as a trade-off. He said, “There is often a dichotomy between whether we should focus on volume or quality and cost. I believe we have to focus on all three: volume, quality, and cost. They have to go together. Once we produce at scale and improve the quality of steel, the cost of production will also come down, making production more competitive and profitable”.

Carbon: The Bill Arrives Mid-Build

The most difficult line on the sheet is decarbonisation, because it falls due while capacity is still being added. The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) entered its payment phase on 1 January 2026. Global Trade Research Initiative has warned that Indian exporters may have to cut prices by 15-22 per cent to let EU buyers absorb the levy.

A report by the think tank Sandbag in August argued that the real impact could be far smaller than feared, and in some scenarios negligible, though it noted that India's emissions-intensive blast-furnace base and its reliance on basic products leave it exposed, especially in long steel.

The domestic constraint is technological and financial. “There are also new technologies such as carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS) and hydrogen injection. However, at this point, it is not yet economically viable to use hydrogen in our blast furnaces or to deploy carbon-capture technologies at scale in India. When we look at European countries, there is significant policy support and subsidies for such technologies,” Panda said.

“The next 10 years will be very challenging for the Indian steel sector, particularly from the perspective of green steel,” he added. Steelmakers must therefore build capacity now while funding costlier technology alongside it, which puts efficiency first. Acharya points to renewable power, process efficiency, resource efficiency and greater circularity.

Financing Sits Under All Four

Each of these pressure points ends in the same place: capital. Capacity, logistics, raw-material security, automation and decarbonisation all draw on the same pool of long-term funding. Capacity expansion, green transition, technology upgradation, AI adoption, automation, logistics and raw material security will require long-term competitive and innovative financing,” Jindal said.

The government's position is that the pace can be sustained. Union Minister of State for Heavy Industries and Steel Bhupathi Raju Srinivasa Varma said India added more than 100 MT of steel capacity over the past decade, compared with the 78 years it took to reach the first 100 MT. The industry shares the optimism, with a condition attached: that government and industry keep moving in step.

“There are challenges, but nothing is insurmountable. With the support of the government, with the steel ministry, the honourable minister is here today with us. So we get all the support and guidance from the ministry, and we are working; industry and the government are working together to achieve 300 million tonnes by 2030-31 and 600 million tonnes by 2047,” Jindal told BW Businessworld.

India has already settled the question of whether it can add tonnes at speed. What remains open is whether those tonnes can be competitive: whether mines and railways can deliver 2 billion tonnes of material at a viable cost, whether domestic coking coal can loosen the grip of a volatile import market, whether quality can rise fast enough to displace imports, and whether the industry can fund decarbonisation without pricing itself out of a crowded world market. For India, the 600 MT target is no longer a test of steelmaking capacity. It is a test of industrial competitiveness, and the answer will be found on the cost sheet.

data.title: Gene Munster Says AI Sell-Off Is About Fear, Not Fundamentals — ‘The Window For Investment Gains Remains Open’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Munster said the recent pullback in AI-focused stocks has made it easy to conclude that the market was in a bubble, with several AI-first companies falling 30%-50% over the past six weeks.
  • He cautioned against drawing that conclusion from the price action alone, noting that the Nasdaq's roughly 16% decline since the start of October was not unprecedented.
  • Munster said that at the heart of the current downturn is anxiety among investors about future earnings, financing conditions and the sustainability of the AI data center buildout.

Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster believes the latest sell-off is being driven more by fear than by deteriorating fundamentals, even as the AI trade comes under mounting pressure, with investors increasingly questioning the scale, financing and long-term returns of the industry's massive infrastructure build-out.

In a note on Friday, Munster argued that investors may be getting caught up in worries about what could go wrong, rather than what AI could ultimately deliver.

Munster Says AI Sell-Off Is About Psychology, Not Fundamentals

Munster said the recent pullback in AI-focused stocks has made it easy to conclude that the market was in a bubble, with several AI-first companies falling 30%-50% over the past six weeks.

However, he cautioned against drawing that conclusion from the price action alone, noting that the Nasdaq's roughly 16% decline since the start of October was not unprecedented. He compared it with the approximately 24% sell-off during the early-2025 DeepSeek shock and tariff uncertainty.

Munster said that at the heart of the current downturn is anxiety among investors about future earnings, financing conditions and whether the data center build-out will continue at the pace previously anticipated.

"The unfortunate answer is that the sell-off will end when [we] have more buyers than sellers," he said.

While acknowledging that the answer may sound flippant, Munster said the market's concerns are increasingly centered on the possibility of multiple quarters of estimate cuts, rather than the fundamentals companies are reporting today.

"At its core, this sell-off is not about fundamentals, it's about psychology," he said.

Munster believes that fear is driving investors to sell as they anticipate the worst, even as the long-term AI opportunity remains intact.

Next Earnings Season Could Help Wall Street Find Its Footing, Says Munster

Munster said investors may have to wait for more clarity on AI spending, financing and data center expansion before sentiment improves meaningfully.

He pointed to late January, when companies begin reporting December-quarter results, as a potential turning point that could offer investors their first meaningful answers about the next phase of the AI build-out.

Among the key concerns are political resistance to data centers, how the infrastructure boom will be financed, Nvidia's role in supporting the ecosystem and the implications of China-related export restrictions.

Munster said even disappointing updates on data center spending could help markets stabilize by giving investors concrete information to assess rather than uncertainty to speculate about.

Munster also highlighted his experience covering Apple Inc. (AAPL) in 2012, when the stock fell roughly 23% from May amid fears of slowing growth and multiple compression. He recalled arguing that fundamentals remained strong, but the stock declined another 8% over the following two months.

"I had the fundamentals right and the stock wrong," he said, adding that "the goal of investing is to get the stocks right."

Dan Ives Also Sees AI Sell-Off As Overreaction

Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives similarly called the AI sell-off one of the most "disconnected" downturns of his career, arguing that stocks are pricing in the possibility that the AI revolution simply goes away.

"I believe we are less than 15% through" the AI opportunity, he said, calling it "a generational opportunity to buy the winners."

Ives added that chip demand remains robust and argued that investors could look back in a year and a half and conclude the market got the sell-off wrong. "And I don't believe it's done, it's just getting started," he said.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 1.11%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) rose 1.53%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) surged 0.94%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) declined over 6% on Friday, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) fell nearly 7%.

Get updates to this story developing directly on Stocktwits.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Tells Traders To Skip Bottom-Fishing And Wait For A Washington 'Bailout'
data.description:
Key points:
  • Arthur Hayes told traders to quit trying to time the market bottom.
  • He had been calling for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to begin printing money.
  • Bitcoin is down more than 6% in 24 hours and about 34% so far this year.

Flop Labs CEO Arthur Hayes told traders to stop trying to pick the market bottom, and wait for a Washington "bailout" instead, asking Bitcoin (BTC) holders to "hold on".

Hayes posted on X as risk assets were sold off. He admitted it is hard to fight the urge to buy a falling market. He wrote, "I succumb often," but he warned followers to "resist the urge to try and pick the bottom," because a bet on the low could go either way.

Alternatively, he can wait for policymakers to intervene. Once the bailout starts it should be bought higher with more conviction by traders, Hayes said. Then he called Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent by nicknames. "Let's go Brrrrr" he concluded, crypto slang for a central bank printing money.

Hayes calls also come as the markets are bracing for tighter policy. Traders now see an 88.6% chance that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its December meeting, according to CME Group's Fed Watch tool. This would lift the benchmark rate by a quarter point to a range of 4% to 4.25%. Higher rates tend to drain cash from risk assets like crypto, which is why Hayes sees little reason to rush in.

On the same day, Hayes posted a picture of Bitcoin dipping, asking people to “hold on” as "Next stop … goblin town", a crypto slang which means a severe bearer market could follow.

Bitcoin Breaks Summer Floor

On Wednesday's New Era Finance podcast, Hayes warned that a burst AI bubble could trigger a global financial crisis and that, if it did, Bitcoin could fall to $10,000. He puts the odds of governments expanding the money supply in a crisis at 99%, which he said could boost Bitcoin and other crypto.

However, Bitcoin dropped over about $3,000 after the Anthropic (ANT) IPO. Bitcoin's price was trading at $57,790, down over 6% in the past 24 hours. The token is now on track for its worst weekly closing streak since 2022.

On Stocktwits, Bitcoin was the top trending ticker among cryptocurrencies at the time of writing. Retail sentiment around BTC dropped to the ‘bearish’ zone from the ‘neutral’ zone amid ‘high’ chatter levels over the past day.

Hayes has previously made the liquidity argument. In August he told investors to buy crypto on the view that Bessent's increased bond buybacks could boost dollar liquidity and push more money into risk assets.

Bitcoin has been down over 34% so far this year and lost over 32% in the last 12 months.

data.title: Rollover Data | What monthly expiry tells you about next month: Shubham Agarwal
data.description:
You bought into the rally a few weeks ago. Nifty has gone up almost in a straight line: ten straight sessions of gains, a nine-month high, and Bank Nifty at a record. Your positions are green.

But the November series ends on 23 November, and one question keeps nagging you. Do you carry these trades into December, or book profits before the retracement everyone is talking about?

After a straight-line rise, a pullback is natural. But not every stock will give up its gains. Some will keep running. Rollover data helps you tell the two apart.

What Is Rollover?

Every futures contract has an expiry date. If a trader wants to keep a position beyond expiry, they close the current month contract and open the same position in the next month. This is called rollover.

Rollover percentage tells you how much of the open interest has shifted to the next series. If a stock has 100 contracts open across November and December, and 70 of them are now in December, rollover is 70%.

High rollover means traders are confident enough to carry their positions forward. Low rollover means they are closing out and walking away.

What Is Rollover Cost?

Rollover cost is the price gap between next month and current month futures, expressed as a percentage.

Rollover Cost = (December Futures – November Futures) ÷ November Futures × 100

Normally, next month futures trade at a small premium because of cost of carry. When rollover cost is higher than usual, traders are paying extra to stay long. That is conviction. When it is low or negative, the rollover is likely coming from short sellers.

This is why rollover percentage alone is not enough. Both buyers and sellers roll their positions. Rollover cost tells you which side is doing it.

Three Rules to Pick Stocks for December

When the market has rallied hard and retracement fear is high, keep a stock on your December list only if it passes all three checks:

1. Existing bullish trend: The stock should already be making higher highs and higher lows. Rollover data confirms a trend; it does not create one.

2. Rollover above its 3-month average: Compare current rollover with the average of the last three expiries. If a stock usually rolls 75% and is now at 85%, traders are carrying more positions than usual.

3. High rollover cost: Rollover cost should be higher than its usual level. This confirms that the extra rollover is coming from buyers willing to pay up to stay long.

When all three line up, strong hands are behind the rally. Such stocks have a better chance of holding up, or even moving higher, while Nifty takes a breather.

When to Stay Away

If a stock has rallied but its rollover is below average, traders are booking profits instead of staying committed. If rollover is high but rollover cost is low or negative, the extra positions are likely shorts betting on a fall. Both are signals to lighten up, not add more.

The Bottom Line

Price shows you where the market has been. Rollover shows you who is willing to stay for what comes next. Before the November series ends, read the data, not just the chart.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Tells Traders To Stop Trying To Pick The Bottom, Wait For A Washington 'Bailout'
data.description:
Key points:
  • Arthur Hayes told traders to quit trying to time the market bottom.
  • He had been calling for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to begin printing money.
  • Bitcoin is down more than 6% in 24 hours and about 34% so far this year.

Flop Labs CEO Arthur Hayes told traders to stop trying to pick the market bottom, and wait for a Washington "bailout" instead, asking Bitcoin (BTC) holders to "hold on".

Hayes posted on X as risk assets were sold off. He admitted it is hard to fight the urge to buy a falling market. He wrote, "I succumb often," but he warned followers to "resist the urge to try and pick the bottom," because a bet on the low could go either way.

Alternatively, he can wait for policymakers to intervene. Once the bailout starts it should be bought higher with more conviction by traders, Hayes said. Then he called Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent by nicknames. "Let's go Brrrrr" he concluded, crypto slang for a central bank printing money.

Hayes calls also come as the markets are bracing for tighter policy. Traders now see an 88.6% chance that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its December meeting, according to CME Group's Fed Watch tool. This would lift the benchmark rate by a quarter point to a range of 4% to 4.25%. Higher rates tend to drain cash from risk assets like crypto, which is why Hayes sees little reason to rush in.

On the same day, Hayes posted a picture of Bitcoin dipping, asking people to “hold on” as "Next stop … goblin town", a crypto slang which means a severe bearer market could follow.

Bitcoin Breaks Summer Floor

On Wednesday's New Era Finance podcast, Hayes warned that a burst AI bubble could trigger a global financial crisis and that, if it did, Bitcoin could fall to $10,000. He puts the odds of governments expanding the money supply in a crisis at 99%, which he said could boost Bitcoin and other crypto.

However, Bitcoin dropped over about $3,000 after the Anthropic (ANT) IPO. Bitcoin's price was trading at $57,790, down over 6% in the past 24 hours. The token is now on track for its worst weekly closing streak since 2022.

On Stocktwits, Bitcoin was the top trending ticker among cryptocurrencies at the time of writing. Retail sentiment around BTC dropped to the ‘bearish’ zone from the ‘neutral’ zone amid ‘high’ chatter levels over the past day.

Hayes has previously made the liquidity argument. In August he told investors to buy crypto on the view that Bessent's increased bond buybacks could boost dollar liquidity and push more money into risk assets.

Bitcoin has been down over 34% so far this year and lost over 32% in the last 12 months.
